title: How Facebook Ads Work: Auctions, Budgets and Ads Manager Setup
summary: Facebook ads run through an auction, a budget and a learning period, all set in Ads Manager. Learn how each part works and why the setup feels complicated.
body_markdown:
## Why Ads Manager feels so complicated


Ads Manager organizes the work in[three levels](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/621956575422138) : campaign, ad set and ad. The campaign holds the objective, the ad set holds the audience, placements, budget and schedule, and the ad holds the creative and the Page and Instagram account it appears from. Every ad in an ad set shares that ad set's settings, so an edit at one level can change how everything beneath it delivers.


On top of that structure, Ads Manager asks for several decisions: which account and business own the ads, the budget type, how long an ad set has to learn, which placements it can use, and which creative enhancements it carries. Each choice is reasonable alone. Together, a small change such as a new ad or a higher budget can change delivery in ways that look like a creative problem.


Automation shifts the work instead of removing it. The system handles more of the audience, placement and bid decisions, and people handle the account structure, the offer, the proof in the creative and the rules for when to change something. If nobody owns those last items, the complexity lands on whoever is reading the dashboard that week.


For a fair test of that complexity, start with one campaign, one objective and one clear event. Add structure only when you can explain what each change did.


## Knowlify: our top pick if you would rather not run Ads Manager yourself


Knowlify is the best fit when the complexity above is the problem and you want both halves handled: the ads and the account. It is a done-for-you AI video ads agency for Facebook and Instagram that delivers about 25 finished ads a week, with the first batch on day 5 and a person checking every ad before delivery. When Meta automates audience, placement and budget, the ads you supply carry more of the work, and a steady supply of finished ads is what Knowlify is built around. It can also run the Meta campaigns end to end, so someone else owns the budget changes, the learning periods and the weekly read of results. It makes[AI UGC](https://knowlify.com/ai-ugc-ads) , 3D and stylized character animation, and AI commercials.


If your team or another buyer already runs media, Knowlify can deliver creative only. Pricing is a custom quote, and media spend is always separate. Where Knowlify runs the account, the guarantee is an agreed target in 30 days, or you don't pay for the month. On creative-only plans, if the ads have not made more than you paid in the first 90 days, you can cancel by email for a full refund (terms on the[pricing and guarantee section](https://knowlify.com/meta-ads-agency#pricing) ). Pick another option if what you need is landing pages or Google, YouTube, TikTok or LinkedIn campaigns, which Knowlify does not build or run.


## What to keep when you hand off


Keep the ad account, pixel and Pages in a business you control, and give any agency access rather than ownership. Decide who approves budget changes and who reads the results each week. For the cost side of that split, read our guide to[how much Facebook ads cost](https://knowlify.com/articles/how-much-do-facebook-ads-cost) , and for choosing a partner, see[how to choose a Facebook ads agency](https://knowlify.com/articles/how-to-choose-a-facebook-ads-agency) .


## Key takeaways


- Facebook ads are sold in an auction scored on bid, expected action rate and ad quality, so creative affects what you pay.
- Daily budgets can flex above the daily amount, Ads Manager enforces a small minimum budget, and a significant edit can restart learning.
- Keep the ad account and pixel in a business you control, whoever runs the ads.
- Knowlify is our first recommendation for done-for-you Meta video ads, but it does not build landing pages or run Google or TikTok ads.


## FAQ


### Why is Facebook Ads Manager so complicated?


Because it asks for several linked decisions at once: account ownership, budget type, the learning period, placements and creative enhancements. Automation removes some manual choices but adds settings to check, such as enhancements that may be on by default. Start with one campaign, one objective and one event, then add complexity only when you can read the results.


### How do Facebook ads work?


Each ad enters an auction, and Meta picks the winner by bid, the estimated chance of the action you optimize for and ad quality. You set a daily or lifetime budget, and delivery follows Meta's budget and learning rules. Creative quality changes what you pay, so the ad is part of the auction.


### Does Facebook have a minimum budget?


Yes, a small one that Ads Manager enforces. Meta's minimum budgets help page says each campaign or ad set needs a minimum budget that varies by country and objective, and Ads Manager shows an alert when a budget is too low. With a cost per result goal, Meta's guidance says the daily budget should be at least five times that goal. Media spend is always separate from any agency fee.


### Who should own the Facebook ad account?


You should. Keep the ad account, pixel and Pages in a business you control, then give an agency access. Meta's business asset documentation says an agency cannot grant access to assets it holds only as an agency, so ownership should stay with the business that pays for the ads.


### What does Knowlify handle for Facebook ads?


Knowlify makes finished AI video ads for Facebook and Instagram, with a person checking every ad, and it can run the Meta campaigns end to end or deliver creative only. It does not build landing pages or run Google, YouTube, TikTok or LinkedIn ads. Get the scope in writing before you compare its quote with an agency.
